newsitem.title: INDIA: India's United Front sees TMC joining government.
newsitem.headline: India's United Front sees TMC joining government.

text.p: India's United Front alliance said on Sunday it was confident that its disgruntled ally, the Tamil Maanila Congress (TMC), would join prime minister-designate Inder Kumar Gujral's new government.
"I am absolutely confident that United Front will be able to prevail upon the TMC to eventually join the government," United Front spokesman Jaipal Reddy told a news conference.
The TMC, miffed that its leader G.K. Moopanar was not chosen to lead the United Front, said on Saturday that it would not join the new government but would lend support to the alliance from outside.
"TMC expressed its resentment at the Steering Committee at the candidature of G.K. Moopanar not being fairly considered by it," Reddy said. "But we hope to bring them back."

Moopanar had been regarded as a front-runner for Deve Gowda's job, but analysts said he was rejected because he was considered too close to the Congress party. The TMC was formed in 1996 by Congress rebels.
Gujral, after a meeting of the decision-making Steering Committee, said he was optimistic the TMC would join the United Front government. "I am moving from hope to optimism," he said.

Finance Minister P. Chidambaram's TMC, a regional party from the southern state of Tamil Nadu, had three other ministers in the outgoing 10-month-old United Front government which lost a parliamentary vote of confidence on April 11.

The party's withdrawal raised doubts over the fate of the 1997/98 (April-March) budget which Chidambaram presented in February and was due to be debated in a special session of parliament from Monday.
But Jaipal Reddy said he was confident Chidambaram would pilot the Finance Bill through parliament.
